item.title: Linux 7.5 removes last MMX-optimized code from kernel
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: The end of an era as Linux 7.5 purges the last 30-year-old Intel MMX optimizations from Pentium age
Linux developers will remove MMX-optimized code from the kernel in version 7.5, set for 2027. The change eliminates the last remaining MMX-specific software RAID XOR code, replacing over 800 lines with 12. Phoronix notes that few users will run modern kernels on Pentium MMX or Pentium II chips by 2026, as most MMX-optimized code was already phased out by 2022. Intel introduced MMX in 1997 as part of Pentium processors, though the acronym’s meaning remains unclear. A court document suggested MMX stood for 'Matrix Math Extensions,' which AMD used to avoid Intel’s trademark. All major x86 processors, including AMD, Centaur, Cyrix, Rise, and Transmeta, eventually supported MMX. After MMX’s rise, AMD introduced 3DNow! and Intel countered with SSE and SSE2. The removal marks a cleanup of legacy code in the Linux kernel.

item.title: British Soldier Hacked After Failing to Remove SIM Card
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: British Soldier on Russian Border Blackmailed, Hacked After Failing to Remove SIM Card
British soldier Daniel Barton Kennedy, 28, was blackmailed and hacked after failing to remove his SIM card as instructed. He reported receiving messages from an unknown party that had obtained nude photographs of him from his phone and identified him on social media. The attacker demanded $135 initially, then $335, prompting Kennedy to seek help from his commanding officer. Captain Farthing, Intelligence Officer of the 1st Battalion of the Duke of Lancaster’s Regiment, explained that failing to follow security protocols could expose military personnel locations, activity patterns, and training details to hostile intelligence. The court proceedings did not confirm the hackers were linked to Russia. Kennedy’s case highlights risks of poor mobile security for NATO forces near Russian borders, where espionage and cyberattacks are suspected. Farthing emphasized that such breaches could aid hostile intelligence collection on NATO capabilities and movements.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: How to use your laptop as a second monitor
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Using a laptop as a second monitor requires specific setup steps across different operating systems. Windows 10/11 users can extend or mirror displays via Miracast over Wi-Fi by enabling Wireless Display settings. Mac users with 2018+ models can use AirPlay for similar functionality. Cross-platform connections between Windows, Mac, or Linux require Deskreen, a Wi-Fi-based tool. HDMI ports on laptops are typically video-out only, so an HDMI-to-USB capture card allows viewing the main display on a second laptop. Gaming via HDMI may offer less lag than wireless methods but still has minor delays. Alternatives include using the laptop as a smart home hub. All methods involve some lag, making them suitable for productivity tasks but not high-performance gaming. Wired HDMI setups are recommended for smoother connections when possible.

item.title: Diamond Foundry creates world's first 200mm single-crystal diamond wafer
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware
Diamond Foundry announced the world’s first 200mm single-crystal diamond (SCD) wafer, marking a breakthrough in semiconductor cooling. The wafer, comparable in size to older semiconductor manufacturing wafers, leverages diamond’s exceptional thermal conductivity—five times that of copper—to address overheating in AI chips. Unlike polycrystalline lab-grown diamonds, the SCD retains electrical insulation while efficiently dissipating heat, reducing hotspots. Diamond Foundry CEO Martin Roscheisen highlighted over a decade of collaboration with scientists and engineers to overcome scaling challenges, calling the achievement a milestone after years of perseverance. The company aims to produce a D300mm SCD wafer by 2030, though the current sample remains unpolished. Other firms, including Akash Systems and De Beers, are also developing diamond-based cooling solutions for AI and high-performance computing. The SCD’s potential could revolutionize thermal management in next-generation electronics.

item.title: NASA Seeks Astronauts for Lunar Missions Under Artemis Program
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: NASA Is Looking for Astronauts to Live and Work on the Moon
NASA seeks astronauts for lunar missions under Artemis program. Applicants must be U.S. citizens with STEM master’s degrees, submitting by December 3, 2026. Selection occurs in late 2027. NASA also opened bids for lunar delivery contracts, including SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Lockheed Martin, excluding Boeing. The Commercial Lunar Payload Services 2 program is a $10 billion, 10-year contract for lunar transport. Elon Musk projected government contracts would make up 5% of SpaceX’s revenue, though NASA’s announcement may shift political dynamics ahead of January’s election.

item.title: Physicists Use Electrical Noise to Solve Superconductor Mystery
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Physicists listened to electrical noise to crack a superconductor mystery
Physicists led by Milan Allan and Ingmar Swart have used electrical noise to investigate why cuprate superconductors operate at higher temperatures. Cuprates, which superconduct at temperatures achievable with liquid nitrogen, remain poorly understood despite decades of research. The team focused on the pseudogap—a state where electrons seem to vanish above the superconducting threshold. Two competing theories exist: one suggests electrons freeze into structures like charge density waves, while another posits they form Cooper pairs, a key feature of superconductivity. Allan noted that while multiple experiments observe missing electrons, they lack conclusive answers. The researchers aimed to directly observe Cooper pairs, which are thought to precede superconductivity. By analyzing electrical noise, they gained insights into this phenomenon, potentially resolving a long-standing debate in condensed matter physics.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: How to safely store a laptop for long-term use
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: The safest way to store your laptop for a long period of time
Storing a laptop long-term requires careful preparation to protect data and hardware. Back up all files before storage to prevent data loss. Lithium-ion batteries need maintenance: charge to 50% before storage, store in temperature-controlled environments away from heat sources and moisture. Periodic checks every six months are recommended to recharge the battery to 50% and prevent over-discharge. Avoid placing heavy objects on the laptop to prevent physical damage. Clean the screen and keyboard before storage to prevent debris buildup. Disconnect from AC power and use original packaging or a case for added protection. Proper storage ensures the laptop remains functional when retrieved.

item.title: NASA Opens Astronaut Program to STEM and Medical Degree Holders
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Got a STEM Degree? NASA Says You Could Become an Astronaut
NASA is accepting applications for its astronaut program, targeting individuals with master’s degrees in STEM fields or medical degrees. Applicants must have a bachelor’s in STEM, two years of PhD study, or complete Test Pilot School. The deadline is December 3, with final selections planned for late 2027. While there are no age restrictions, past recruits ranged from 26 to 46. Candidates must be free of medical conditions that could impair spaceflight and have at least three years of professional experience post-degree. Medical degree holders include doctors, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants. Applications are open to U.S. citizens.

item.title: Ukraine develops combat robots for underground pipeline warfare
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Ukraine builds combat robots to hunt Russian troops in underground gas pipelines
Ukraine is developing combat robots to operate in underground gas pipelines, where Russian troops have attempted to bypass defenses. The 2nd National Guard Corps, Khartiia, modified unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) for narrow spaces, following Operation Veles, an underground assault near Kupiansk that advanced 15 kilometers through pipelines. The operation reportedly killed over 100 Russian soldiers and captured 30, though figures are unverified. Commander Matematyk, of the Lava Unmanned Systems Regiment, emphasized the need for new technologies to address underground warfare challenges. The robots, adapted from existing systems, must navigate tight spaces while retaining combat capabilities. Commercial underground machinery is not designed for military use. Khartiia is expanding robotic systems for dangerous subterranean environments, as underground operations restrict visibility and mobility. Ukraine has increased reliance on unmanned systems, including AI-controlled drones and autonomous vehicles. Russia tested AI-powered Shahed drones using Nvidia tech, while its Shturm tanks faced command connection issues during exercises. The project follows Russian use of pipeline networks for infiltration, including an August 2025 attempt reported by Deepstate.

item.title: Second Circuit Denies Kalshi, Coinbase Interim Relief in State Gambling Cases
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite Original headline: Second Circuit denies Kalshi and Coinbase interim relief against New York and Connecticut
The Second Circuit denied Kalshi and Coinbase interim relief from New York and Connecticut, allowing both states to proceed with state-court cases against the companies' sports event contracts. The ruling, issued after a hearing, found the companies failed to meet the burden for an injunction pending appeal. New York and Connecticut can now enforce gambling laws, pursuing suits to block the contracts. Gaming attorney Daniel Wallach called the decision a major win for the states. Kalshi had already lost at the district level, with federal courts rejecting preliminary injunctions in July 2026 and August 2026. New York sued KalshiEX in July 2026, while Connecticut filed a lawsuit in August 2026. The decision deepens a circuit split over regulation of prediction markets, with the Third Circuit previously ruling in favor of Kalshi. The CFTC has also sued multiple states over enforcement actions, seeking exclusive federal jurisdiction. The outcome affects state sportsbook markets and CFTC authority, with New Jersey’s petition for Supreme Court review pending.

item.title: Japanese arcades face blackout after Sega server hack disrupts online gaming
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Japanese arcades suffer week-long blackout following Sega server hack
Japanese arcades faced a week-long blackout after Sega's server hack disrupted online services for its and Bandai Namco games. ALL.net, Sega's arcade network, suspended operations on November 1 after detecting unauthorized third-party access to its servers. The outage affected titles like Initial D The Arcade, Maimai, and Aiko no Tatsujin, with online play and card systems partially restored starting November 2. Sega's online services remain unavailable, though a news bulletin is scheduled for November 10. Personal data and billing information were not compromised. Classic offline arcade machines and rival companies like Taito and Konami, which use separate networks, were unaffected. ALL.net apologized for the disruption and requested additional time for safety checks before full service recovery.

item.title: Apple's HomeView may support chatbots via iOS 27.3 beta code
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Chatbots might be coming to Apple’s HomeView
Code in the iOS 27.3 beta indicates Apple may add chatbot support to its HomeView smart home hub. A 'Conversational Apps' flag suggests integration of AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude. The beta also includes bidirectional audio routing and anti-spoofing protections requiring iPhone authentication after three failed attempts. A lockout system imposes longer wait times, starting at one hour for the second attempt and reaching eight hours by the fourth. These features, however, remain unannounced by Apple, with no release timeline provided. The changes are part of ongoing beta updates but are not yet fully implemented.

item.title: Ukrainian receiver intercepts Russian drone video signals up to six miles
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Pocket-sized Ukrainian receiver intercepts Russian strike drone video feeds up to six miles away
CODE380, a Kyiv-based radio manufacturer, developed the D·Vision SDR, a software-defined radio that intercepts analog video signals from Russian strike drones. The device can scan frequencies from 500 MHz to 8.7 GHz, detecting signals up to six miles away on the 540 MHz to 6 GHz band. Weighing 10 ounces, it is lighter than competitors like the 2-pound Vydun 7.5 or 23-ounce Chuyka 3.0. Presidential advisor Serhii Beskrestnov noted these receivers cover the 4.1 to 4.5 GHz band used by Russian Molniya drones but warned they should not be relied on alone. He emphasized that most detectors struggle with these frequencies. The D·Vision SDR is designed for analog signals but claims digital UAV detection, though currently focused on DJI drones. It may require downed units to identify Russian drone hardware. Fiber optic drones, however, remain undetectable due to their physical connections.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Five Docker Containers for Secure Homelab Internet Exposure
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: 5 Docker containers I'd install before exposing my homelab to the internet
Five Docker containers are recommended for securely exposing a homelab to the internet. Caddy handles reverse proxying and HTTPS with automatic certificate management. Dockhand provides a web interface for Docker environment management, combining logging and image update features. CrowdSec detects malicious traffic and blocks IPs using threat intelligence. Tailscale enables private network access to homelab services without public exposure. Uptime Kuma monitors service availability with HTTP/TCP checks and status pages. The author advises configuring these tools before deploying applications, emphasizing backups for Compose files and persistent volumes to simplify future migrations or rebuilds.

item.title: Autonomous Farming Combines AI, Sensors to Transform Agriculture
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: The rise of the autonomous farm
Autonomous farming faces unique challenges due to variable weather, soil, and crop conditions. John Deere’s Intelligent Solutions Group leads in developing AI-driven systems that use cameras, computer vision, and neural networks to navigate fields, distinguish obstacles, and make real-time decisions. These systems enable tractors to operate without continuous human oversight, shifting farmers’ roles from machine operators to data managers. Cloud platforms allow remote monitoring and adjustments, enhancing visibility across operations. Adoption requires compatibility with both new and existing machinery, as full autonomy emerges incrementally through integrated technology. While automation handles execution, farmers retain control over strategic decisions, using data to manage complexity. The shift emphasizes combining AI, sensing, and human judgment to improve efficiency without replacing human expertise. Autonomous tractors can handle tasks like tillage while freeing farmers to focus on broader management, demonstrating that the future of farming is not about removing people but enhancing their capabilities through technology.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Georgia Tech student claims 491 mph drone speed record
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: US college student builds 'Reaper' drone — which he says set a new world record speed of 491mph
Georgia Tech student Tomas Salvo claims his homemade Reaper drone reached 491 mph, potentially setting a new world record for remotely controlled aircraft. The $13,000 jet-powered model, which carried a 2.6-pound payload, sustained the speed for four minutes across three prototypes. Salvo developed the aircraft independently since February 2025, using a 250-newton turbojet, 3D-printed titanium exhaust nozzle, and carbon-fibre construction. The drone can climb to 6,600 feet in 20 seconds and travel 31 miles at max speed. While the performance exceeds the 2017 465 mph record, it falls short of the Boom Supersonic competition's Mach 1 requirement. Salvo plans to refine the design to surpass 500 mph. His project attracted attention from Pentagon officials, including Prescott Paulin, who invited him to visit the department. The Boom Prize offers $750,000 and shares for supersonic flights, but Salvo's current speed does not qualify. The competition excludes rocket propulsion and requires air-breathing engines, with rules restricting professional involvement.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Homelabber Runs 2.8T-Param AI Model on Optane Memory Without GPU
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Homelabber uses second-gen Optane memory sticks to run a 2.8-trillion-parameter AI model on CPU alone
A homelabber ran Moonshot AI’s 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 model on second-gen Optane PMem 200 memory using a 40-core 3rd-gen Xeon Scalable CPU without a GPU. The build achieved 0.85 tokens per second with 1-bit quantization, slower than a prior 1-trillion-parameter model running on a GPU. The project requires active DIMM cooling, with dual 12W fans to manage heat from Optane modules, which reached 12W or 15W per stick. Intel’s specs recommend 2.4–2.7 m/s airflow for cooling, typical in data centers. The build faces thermal limits, with throttling at 83°C and shutdown at 85°C, compared to DDR4’s 85°C and 95°C range. DRAM prices are high, making Optane a cheaper alternative for home use. The builder plans to add GPUs and use DRAM as a faster tier alongside Optane, with further benchmarks pending.

item.title: Epic Games Launcher to Support SteamOS and Steam Decks
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Epic Games Launcher is coming to SteamOS
Epic Games confirmed its Linux launcher will support SteamOS and Steam Decks. Communications Director Jake Jones stated the launcher is in preview and will support multiple Linux distributions, including SteamOS, Fedora, Cachy, Omarchy, and others. The company plans to restore AppImage support this month while testing packaging formats. However, Fortnite's availability on SteamOS remains uncertain due to ongoing challenges with Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) Linux v2 support. Epic Games noted Steam Deck lacks the required features for EAC v2 but is in talks with Valve to address the issue in the future. The confirmation comes after initial announcements about investigating SteamOS compatibility earlier this year.

item.title: PocketBar lets Mac users run Android apps without emulator hassle
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: PocketBar lets you use your favorite Android apps on Mac without the emulator hassle
PocketBar enables Mac users to run Android apps without emulator visibility. The app hides the emulator, launching each Android app in its own window alongside native macOS apps. It supports Android 11 through 16, with app sources including F-Droid, IzzyOnDroid, Aurora Store, and sideloaded APKs. Google Play is optional but requires 2GB of storage. Security features include Touch ID for private apps and ad/tracker blocking. Compatible apps include YouTube, Instagram, Signal, and Telegram, though X, WhatsApp, banking apps, and games may have issues. PocketBar is free to try on Apple Silicon Macs with macOS 14 or later. PocketBar Pro, costing €9.99, adds screen recording, app backups, and unlimited menu bar shortcuts. No subscription is required, and all updates in the 1.x series are included.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Laptop fans spin up due to dust or background tasks
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Why your laptop fans spin up without any warning
Laptop fans may spin up unexpectedly due to dust buildup or intensive background processes. Users should check airflow by placing the laptop on a flat surface and cleaning vents with compressed air or a microfiber cloth. If fans continue to overheat, investigate background tasks via Task Manager on Windows or Activity Monitor on Mac. Disable unnecessary startup programs and processes to reduce CPU load. Avoid randomly closing processes to prevent system crashes. For advanced users, dismantling the laptop to clean fans may be necessary, though warranty terms should be checked before attempting repairs. Both operating systems offer tools to identify resource-heavy processes, allowing users to optimize performance and minimize fan noise.

item.title: PC RAM Lifespan: How Long Can You Expect It to Last?
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: How long can you expect your PC RAM to last?
PC RAM lifespan ranges from 3 to 15 years, depending on usage and quality. Manufacturing defects, workload intensity, overclocking, ambient heat, and static shocks can shorten longevity. DDR4 remains sufficient for most tasks, while DDR5 offers performance gains in gaming and AI processing. CPU and motherboard compatibility dictate RAM upgrades, as newer systems often lack DDR4 support. Users with heavy workloads or overclocking may face reliability issues, but average users can rely on existing RAM for years. PCWorld notes that material degradation is unlikely to cause failure before a system upgrade. Quantity often matters more than speed, with 32GB DDR4 outperforming 16GB DDR5 in multitasking. Lifespan isn't the primary concern; performance bottlenecks and compatibility with evolving hardware are critical factors.

item.title: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 Balances Factions for Intuitive Play
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 creative director explains how King Art balances RTS factions 'organically' so 'players who do not know the faction still intuitively play them the right way' — 'This is also an ongoing process'
Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 creative director Jan Theysen explained how King Art Games balanced the four playable factions—Space Marines, Orks, Necrons, and Adeptus Mechanicus—without compromising their core traits. Theysen emphasized identifying each faction's 'feeling' to ensure players intuitively grasp their playstyle even without prior knowledge. For example, Space Marines are costly and upgraded, while Orks are cheap and numerous but fragile. Testing with AI bots and real players revealed how factions naturally influence strategy, like Ork players focusing on mass units versus Space Marine players prioritizing individual units. Theysen noted adjustments are ongoing, as player feedback often exposes unanticipated imbalances. 'This is also an ongoing process,' he said, adding that real players 'come up with stuff you never thought about,' requiring continuous tweaks to maintain fairness while preserving faction identity.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: United Airlines offers free Spotify access on select flights
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Some United Airlines flights now let you sign into Spotify on your flight — and its' totally free
United Airlines is rolling out Spotify access on select flights via its in-flight entertainment system. Passengers can log into their Spotify accounts using the plane's Wi-Fi network and a QR code scan, granting access to playlists and podcasts without paying for in-flight internet. The feature initially requires a Starlink connection and will expand to more flights by 2027. This follows a prior partnership that offered limited Spotify content on in-flight screens. Users do not need to pay for Wi-Fi to access Spotify, though the service’s availability for non-premium accounts isn’t specified. The system requires wired headphones or compatible receivers for wireless devices. The update aims to enhance in-flight entertainment options, allowing passengers to stream music or podcasts without using their phones. The feature is part of United’s broader collaboration with Spotify to improve passenger experience during flights.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: ChatGPT fixed three major Windows issues by analyzing event logs
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: I gave ChatGPT my Windows logs, and it fixed 3 major problems I'd overlooked
ChatGPT identified and resolved three critical issues on a user's ASUS TUF Gaming laptop by analyzing Windows event logs. The AI flagged a BitLocker encryption discrepancy, revealing the drive was 100% encrypted but lacked a recovery key. It provided commands to generate and back up a recovery password, resolving persistent Event ID 24641 errors. ChatGPT also diagnosed a crashing RefreshRateService linked to conflicting OEM bloatware, guiding the user to disable the service without disrupting G-Helper functionality. Additionally, it clarified a TPM-related error was a software handshake issue, not hardware failure, after running diagnostic commands. The user emphasized verifying AI suggestions before system changes, highlighting the value of leveraging LLMs for troubleshooting without IT expertise.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Users can disable Google Health's AI Coach feature
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Don't like Google Health's AI Coach? Here's how to turn it off
Google Health users can disable the AI Coach feature by canceling their Premium subscription or toggling it off via privacy controls. The AI Coach, powered by Gemini, offers personalized guidance, meal logging, and workout adjustments but can be turned off without deleting data. Users can access privacy settings through the app by navigating to 'Your data in Google Health' or 'Google Health settings' to manage coaching features. Disabling the coach removes personalized insights, recommendations, and the 'Ask Coach' function, though manual logging remains available. Users may opt to turn off notifications instead of the feature entirely. The AI Coach can be reactivated by tapping the 'Ask Coach' button, though this requires a different menu path than initially disabling it. Some users find the coach helpful for tracking fitness and nutrition but consider its repetitive advice intrusive. The feature is available in the Premium tier but not the free version.

item.title: New HDDs Show 1.5% Failure Rate, 30% Fail Without Warning
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: A sample of over 5,000 drives reveals one problem with new HDDs
Backblaze data shows 1.5% of new HDDs fail within their first year, with 30% of those failures occurring without warning. The average lifespan of failed drives is 807 days. Common causes include production defects, power issues, and internal system damage. Seagate, Hitachi, and Western Digital models show varying reliability. HDDs remain cheaper than SSDs for high-capacity storage, though SSDs offer faster performance. Drives over seven years old face higher failure risks, prompting recommendations for replacement schedules or supplemental storage. Emerging HDD technologies like SMR and HAMR are under observation but not yet widely used. Experts advise combining cloud, local, and off-site storage to mitigate data loss risks. HDDs remain viable for cost-sensitive applications but require proactive monitoring and redundancy strategies.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: User Adds $30 USB Expansion Card to Proxmox Node
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: I replaced my desktop's missing USB ports with one $30 expansion card
A user upgraded their Lenovo ThinkCentre M910s desktop, used as a Proxmox node, by adding a FebSmart FS-U4L-Pro USB expansion card. The machine had limited USB ports, so the card provided four USB-A 3.0 ports via PCIe 2.0 x1. The card uses a Renesas controller with Linux kernel support, eliminating the need for extra drivers. Installation was straightforward, fitting into a PCIe 3.0 slot. Testing showed transfer speeds of 350-420 MB/s with a USB 3.0 SSD, but an NVMe drive didn't improve speeds due to PCIe bandwidth limits. The user chose the card for its balance of performance and cost, avoiding overprovisioning for the setup. The card offers reliable connectivity without replacing the motherboard, making it a practical upgrade for compact Proxmox nodes.

item.title: Google adds real-time threat checks to Chrome's Incognito mode
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Chrome’s Incognito mode has a security blind spot, but Google is plugging the hole now
Google is addressing a security gap in Chrome’s Incognito mode by extending real-time Safe Browsing protections to private browsing. Current Incognito mode relies on outdated local threat lists updated every 30-60 minutes, which may miss recently emerged malicious websites. A new Chromium development aims to apply real-time threat checks to both Incognito and Guest modes, improving defenses against phishing and malware. Privacy concerns are mitigated by keeping temporary security keys in memory rather than storing them locally. Standard Protection uses privacy servers to hide IP addresses during checks, while Enhanced Protection shares more data with Google. Incognito mode does not provide anonymity, as websites and network admins can still track activity. The feature remains experimental, disabled by default, with no public release date announced.

item.title: Microsoft Adds Checkbox to Disable Sticky Keys Dialog in Windows 11
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Microsoft Is Finally Making Windows Sticky Keys Dialogs Less Sticky
Microsoft is adding a checkbox in Windows 11 to permanently disable the Sticky Keys activation dialog. The change was spotted in an Insider Beta Preview Build, allowing users to tick 'Never turn on Sticky Keys with this shortcut' to eliminate the pop-up. Previously, disabling the feature required multiple steps. Sticky Keys, an accessibility tool enabling multiple modifier keys without holding them all down, remains a helpful feature. However, the dialog has been a nuisance for users who don't need it, such as during gaming or typing. Windows engineer Jen Gentleman shared the update via Twitter. This change aligns with broader Windows improvements, including better search functionality and semantic search in Photos, highlighted by Microsoft VP Navjot Virk. While the update addresses a minor UI quirk, its impact on user retention against competitors like Linux or macOS remains uncertain.

item.title: Media industry continues shift to social video formats
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: There’s no slowing down media’s pivot-to-video 2.0
Media organizations are accelerating their shift to social video formats as platforms like TikTok, YouTube, and Instagram dominate user engagement. This follows a previous failed pivot to video in the mid-2010s, which saw inflated metrics and layoffs due to unmet revenue goals. Now, news outlets are adapting by creating vertical video content, partnering with creators, and experimenting with new formats like TikTok-style clips and longer-form programming. The Washington Post, CNN, and The New York Times have launched social video initiatives, while platforms like YouTube and Instagram are pushing toward horizontal, higher-quality content. Nielsen reports YouTube commands 16% of TV viewing, and 20% of Americans get news from TikTok. Critics note that views alone don’t translate to revenue, with platforms measuring engagement by impressions rather than actual watch time. Newsrooms face pressure to balance authenticity with platform demands, as creators and platforms increasingly shape content trends. The industry now grapples with evolving formats, from short clips to longform streaming, as tech companies seek to retain users across devices.

item.title: White Cameras Above Traffic Lights Monitor Traffic Flow
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Those white cameras mounted above traffic lights serve a little-known purpose
Cameras mounted above traffic lights primarily monitor traffic flow rather than track individual drivers. Unlike automatic license plate readers (ALPRs) like Flock, which are used for law enforcement and face privacy concerns, these cameras focus on real-time traffic data to manage congestion. They help transportation departments adjust signal timings, detect accidents, and track long-term traffic patterns. Some systems use video feeds, radar, infrared cameras, and electromagnetic detectors to sense vehicle presence. Local laws determine camera types and uses, with many cameras linked to automated signaling systems that change light cycles based on traffic. While ALPRs remain controversial, cameras above traffic lights are typically designed to keep roads moving, not to capture evidence for enforcement.

item.title: Apple to Boost Siri with Agentic AI by Next Year
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo, The Verge, PCMag Original headline: Apple Aims to Enhance Siri with Agentic AI Features by Next Year
Apple is advancing Siri's development to include agentic AI features by next year, according to reports. CEO John Ternus has urged Craig Federighi, senior VP of Software Engineering, to accelerate work on autonomous AI capabilities. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman noted Ternus has grown frustrated with slow AI integration, prompting internal meetings to push for faster progress. Federighi, skeptical of AI’s broader implications, faces challenges including potential departure of Mike Rockwell, vice president of Siri engineering. Rockwell, who led the Vision Pro headset project, reportedly feels undervalued for his work on Siri’s AI improvements. His exit would shift responsibilities to Amar Subramanya and Sebastien Marineau. The changes aim to enhance Siri’s ability to handle complex, ongoing tasks beyond its current request-based model.
